report_text: Finance mentioned revenue felt slightly off this week. Can you check whether anything is wrong?

hypotheses.description: cloudpay_v2 migration (2026-08-07 cutover) introduced a unit/semantic defect (e.g. minor-currency units, duplicates, bad currency codes) that distorts revenue.
stg_fx_rates forward-fill is masking a stale FX feed (raw_fx_rates stops 2026-08-05), materially understating USD-normalized revenue for 08-06..08-09.
The inner JOIN in fct_revenue drops orders whose currency/day has no FX row, silently losing revenue after the cutover.

data.sql:
-- stg_orders: cleaned order stream.
-- Excludes cancelled and refunded orders from the revenue path.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_orders AS
SELECT
    order_id,
    CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS order_ts,
    CAST(CAST(order_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    customer_id,
    currency,
    CAST(amount AS DOUBLE) AS amount,
    payment_processor,
    status
FROM raw.raw_orders
WHERE status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'refunded');

-- fct_revenue: daily revenue fact, USD-normalized via stg_fx_rates.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.fct_revenue AS
SELECT
    o.order_day AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    ROUND(SUM(o.amount * fx.usd_rate), 2) AS revenue_usd,
    ROUND(AVG(o.amount * fx.usd_rate), 2) AS aov_usd,
    ROUND(MEDIAN(o.amount * fx.usd_rate), 2) AS aov_median_usd
FROM staging.stg_orders o
JOIN staging.stg_fx_rates fx
  ON fx.rate_day = o.order_day
 AND fx.currency = o.currency
GROUP BY o.order_day
ORDER BY o.order_day;

-- stg_fx_rates: daily USD conversion rates, forward-filled over a full day
-- spine so that days where the upstream feed is missing carry the last known
-- rate forward. USD is added explicitly at 1.0.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE staging.stg_fx_rates AS
WITH bounds AS (
    SELECT MIN(order_day) AS d0, MAX(order_day) AS d1
    FROM staging.stg_orders
),
day_spine AS (
    SELECT CAST(r.range AS DATE) AS rate_day
    FROM bounds b,
         LATERAL range(CAST(b.d0 AS TIMESTAMP), CAST(b.d1 AS TIMESTAMP) + INTERVAL 1 DAY, INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS r
),
currencies AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT currency FROM raw.raw_fx_rates
),
spine AS (
    SELECT d.rate_day, c.currency
    FROM day_spine d CROSS JOIN currencies c
),
joined AS (
    SELECT
        s.rate_day,
        s.currency,
        CAST(r.usd_rate AS DOUBLE) AS usd_rate_raw
    FROM spine s
    LEFT JOIN raw.raw_fx_rates r
      ON CAST(r.rate_day AS DATE) = s.rate_day AND r.currency = s.currency
),
filled AS (
    SELECT
        rate_day,
        currency,
        LAST_VALUE(usd_rate_raw IGNORE NULLS) OVER (
            PARTITION BY currency
            ORDER BY rate_day
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS usd_rate
    FROM joined
)
SELECT rate_day, currency, usd_rate FROM filled
UNION ALL
SELECT rate_day, 'USD' AS currency, 1.0 AS usd_rate FROM day_spine
ORDER BY rate_day, currency;

-- exec_revenue_metric: single-row executive KPI.
-- trailing_28d_median_revenue uses days -35..-8 relative to kpi_day (a stable
-- pre-cutover window) so the reference is robust to recent turbulence.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE marts.exec_revenue_metric AS
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(day) AS kpi_day FROM marts.fct_revenue
),
current_rev AS (
    SELECT f.day AS kpi_day, f.revenue_usd AS revenue
    FROM marts.fct_revenue f, latest l
    WHERE f.day = l.kpi_day
),
trailing_window AS (
    SELECT MEDIAN(f.revenue_usd) AS trailing_28d_median_revenue
    FROM marts.fct_revenue f, latest l
    WHERE f.day BETWEEN l.kpi_day - 35 AND l.kpi_day - 8
)
SELECT
    c.kpi_day,
    c.revenue,
    ROUND(t.trailing_28d_median_revenue, 2) AS trailing_28d_median_revenue,
    ROUND(c.revenue / t.trailing_28d_median_revenue, 4) AS anomaly_ratio
FROM current_rev c, trailing_window t;

final_summary:
The reported "revenue feels slightly off" is a day-of-week composition artifact, not a data defect.

1) NO DIVERGENCE FROM BASELINE. All 14 most-recent days show revenue_ratio = 1.000 and aov_ratio = 1.000 against the committed healthy baseline, with order counts matching exactly [ev_1267f1dfd7]. The full invariant suite passes 32/32 with zero failures [ev_efacfdb817].

2) THE HEADLINE DIP IS NORMAL VARIANCE. The KPI's anomaly_ratio of 0.9327 on 2026-08-09 is not an outlier: across 89 days of history the ratio of daily revenue to its own trailing-28d median has sd = 0.129, range 0.733-1.298, and 27 of 89 days (30%) were WORSE than 0.9327 [ev_ad31cfcbe0]. Today sits ~0.5 sd below the mean.

3) THE APPARENT SOFTNESS IS CALENDAR, NOT DATA. The last three days are Fri/Sat/Sun. Against day-of-week averages: Friday 08-07 = 26,557 vs Friday pre-average 31,619 (sd 3,298, i.e. -1.5 sd, within noise), but Saturday 08-08 = 27,384 vs Saturday average 25,596 and Sunday 08-09 = 27,373 vs Sunday average 25,195 — two of the three days are ABOVE their day-of-week norm [ev_8439cc3fd6]. The KPI's trailing-median reference window (days -35..-8) blends all seven weekdays, so any weekend-heavy tail reads low by construction [ev_b3304e7436].

4) THE ONE REAL CHANGE IS A DOCUMENTED BENIGN MIGRATION. On 2026-08-07 the payment mix cut over entirely from legacy_pos/shopgate to cloudpay_v2 [ev_1f844465ec], exactly as the DataHub contract predicts: raw_orders.payment_processor documents cloudpay_v2 as a "new provider being rolled out in early August 2026 per the payments-platform runbook" [ev_4e85670b27]. The cohort is contract-clean: 1062 rows / 1062 distinct order_ids (no duplicates), 0 amounts violating the v1.3 two-decimal major-units rule, 0 non-positive amounts, 0 invalid ISO-4217 codes, 0 null customers, and mean amount 79.59 vs legacy_pos 79.99 / shopgate 80.93 — ruling out a minor-units (cents) error, which would have shown a 100x shift [ev_72c23b57bd]. Raw-to-staging counts reconcile exactly (334/349/327 completed = staged) so no rows are lost [ev_13ee4e01ce, ev_4b31e5fe55]. Revenue per order is flat across the cutover: 80.56 post vs 81.14 prior-30d vs 80.46 earlier (-0.7%, noise) [ev_3ab62e908f]. Per the rule that a benign migration which does not distort metrics is not an incident, this is a clean cutover.

NO REPAIR PROPOSED: there is no defect to fix, and changing the pipeline to force the KPI upward would fabricate an incident and corrupt correct data.

FOLLOW-UP (hygiene ticket, NOT an incident): raw_fx_rates stops delivering at 2026-08-05, so 08-06..08-09 run on forward-filled rates [ev_0c124d984f, ev_d4a460f7c8]. This is the documented intended behavior of stg_fx_rates, and its magnitude is negligible — non-USD is only 3.3-7.7% of daily revenue [ev_1089df715d] and FX drift averages 0.08-0.15%/day (max 0.31%) [ev_3d444d7f8f], bounding the error near 0.04% of total revenue (~$10/day), roughly 150x too small to explain the reported dip. I recommend a freshness alert on raw_fx_rates so the forward-fill cannot silently mask a longer outage, plus a day-of-week-aware or 7-day-lagged reference in exec_revenue_metric to stop this false positive from recurring.
